'''Justin Anthony Hamilton''' (born April 1, 1990)''[http://i.cdn.turner.com/nba/nba/.element/media/2.0/teamsites/heat/media/pdf/2013-14_heat_media_guide.pdf 2013-14 Miami Heat Media Guide]'', p. 79. is a Croatian-American professional [[basketball]] coach and former player who is a video coordinator and player development coach for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]] and the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. ==College career== Hamilton played [[college basketball]] for the Iowa State Cyclones from 2008 to 2010 under Greg McDermott, and Louisiana State University during the 2011–12 season under Trent Johnson after being required to redshirt the 2010–11 season due to NCAA transfer requirements.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}} ==Professional career== Hamilton was selected with the 45th overall in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He was then traded to the [[Miami Heat]] for the rights of [[Arnett Moultrie]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft/2012/prospects/justin-hamilton/ |title=Prospect Profile: Justin Hamilton – NBA.com |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=June 29, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120702103445/http://www.nba.com/draft/2012/prospects/justin-hamilton/ |archive-date=July 2, 2012 |url-status=dead }} In August 2012, Hamilton signed with [[KK Cibona]] and has expressed a desire to play for the [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatian national basketball team]]. In January 2013, he moved to [[BK VEF Rīga|VEF Rīga]] after an agreement with Cibona allowed him to switch clubs.[http://sportacentrs.com/basketbols/eirokausi/24012013-vef_riga_pievienosies_centra_speletajs_dz "VEF Rīga" pievienosies centra spēlētājs Džastins Hemiltons] He left the team in May. On September 10, 2013, he signed with the [[Miami Heat]].[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14233 Miami Heat sign Eric Griffin and Justin Hamilton] However, he was waived on October 26.[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14668 Miami Heat waive Eric Griffin and Justin Hamilton] On October 31, 2013, he was acquired by the Sioux Falls Skyforce.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/1314_training_camp_invitees_131031.html Skyforce Announces Initial 2013-14 Training Camp Invitees] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107095620/http://www.nba.com/dleague/siouxfalls/1314_training_camp_invitees_131031.html |date=November 7, 2015 }} On February 3, 2014, Hamilton was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |date=February 7, 2014 }} On March 4, 2014, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20140305043943/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/cats-sign-hamilton-10-day-contract|title=Cats Sign Hamilton to 10-Day Contract}} He made his only appearance for the Bobcats on March 8 in a loss to [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. On March 14, 2014, he signed with the [[Miami Heat]] for the rest of the season.[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-justin-hamilton HEAT Signs Justin Hamilton] On March 20, 2014, he was assigned to the Sioux Falls Skyforce.[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/justin-hamilton-join-skyforce Justin Hamilton to Join Skyforce] On March 24, 2014, he was recalled by the Heat. The Heat made the [[2014 NBA Finals]], where they lost to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in five games. Hamilton did not play a game in the 2014 playoffs for Miami. On February 19, 2015, Hamilton was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-complete-three-team-trade-miami-phoenix|title=Pelicans Complete Three-Team Trade with Miami, Phoenix|date=February 19, 2015|work=NBA.com}} On March 3, 2015, he was waived by the Pelicans before appearing in a game for them.[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-justin-hamilton Pelicans Waive Justin Hamilton] Two days later, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-awarded-justin-hamilton-waivers|title=Timberwolves Awarded Justin Hamilton Off Waivers|date=March 5, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=March 5, 2015}} On July 27, 2015, Hamilton signed a one-year deal with [[Valencia BC|Valencia]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[Eurocup Basketball|Eurocup]].{{cite news|title=Valencia adds big men Hamilton, Shurna|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/68bfneijtemf3kry|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150730004612/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/68bfneijtemf3kry|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 30, 2015|access-date=July 27, 2015|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 27, 2015}} Valencia reached the league's semi-finals and Hamilton earned [[All-Liga ACB Team|All-Liga ACB First Team]] honours as the top power forward in the league.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}} On July 11, 2016, Hamilton signed a multi-year contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2016/07/11/brooklyn-nets-sign-justin-hamilton|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Justin Hamilton|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 11, 2016|access-date=July 11, 2016}} He made his debut for the Nets in their season opener on October 26, 2016, against the [[Boston Celtics]]. In 25 minutes off the bench, he recorded a career-high 19 points and 10 rebounds in a 122–117 loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899380|title=Thomas scores 25, Celtics fight off Nets 122-117|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 27, 2016}} On December 20, 2016, he grabbed a career-high 11 rebounds in a 116–104 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899862|title=Lowry, Powell lead Raptors to 116-104 win over Nets|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2016|access-date=December 21, 2016}} On July 13, 2017, Hamilton was traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[DeMarre Carroll]], a future first-round pick and a future second-round pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/raptors-acquire-hamilton-from-nets|title=Raptors Acquire Hamilton From Nets|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2017|access-date=July 13, 2017}} The next day, he was waived by the Raptors.{{cite web|last=Murphy|first=Blake|url=http://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2017/07/14/raptors-waive-justin-hamilton/|title=Raptors waive Justin Hamilton|work=RaptorsRepublic.com|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=July 14, 2017}} On July 22, 2017, Hamilton signed with the [[Beijing Ducks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/242028/justin-hamilton-signs-with-beijing-ducks.html?rel=related_desktop Justin Hamilton signs with Beijing Ducks][https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/justin-hamilton-headed-to-china/ Justin Hamilton: Headed to China] On August 14, 2022, he has signed with [[Bàsquet Manresa|Baxi Manresa]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1377733/manresa-adds-justin-hamilton-basketball-champions-league/|title=Manresa bolsters squad with Justin Hamilton|last=|first=|date=August 14, 2022|website=|publisher=Eurohoops|language=En|access-date=August 14, 2022}} ==Coaching career== On August 31, 2024, Hamilton retired from professional basketball to join the [[Golden State Warriors]] as a video coordinator and player development coach.{{cite web|title=Warriors Add Jerry Stackhouse and Terry Stotts as Assistant Coaches|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-add-jerry-stackhouse-and-terry-stotts-as-assistant-coaches-20240927|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2024|access-date=September 27, 2024}}
